speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
text: asked the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance whether the Ministry will consider reducing the property tax rates for owner-occupied private residential properties occupied by elderly retirees who have been unduly affected by the escalating rental of neighbouring units, which disproportionately affects their properties' annual value.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
text: asked the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (a) for the past three years, what is the annual average rate of increase of property tax for owner-occupied private properties in both prime and non-prime locations respectively; (b) whether the annual property tax computation is influenced by the use of neighbouring properties for rental income; and (c) whether the Ministry will review the property tax computation for prime locations so that owners of these owner-occupied homes, especially retirees, are not unfairly penalised.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: Mr Speaker, may I have your permission to answer Question Nos 3 and 4 together?

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: PT payable is based on the applicable PT rate, applied to the Annual Value, or AV, of the property, where AV is a proxy for the property value and, thus, the owner's wealth.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: In line with the wealth tax intent of PT, the PT on residential properties is taxed on a progressive schedule.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Properties with AVs of up to $8,000 pay no PT, while properties with higher AVs pay PT at progressively higher rates of taxation.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Owner-occupied residential properties enjoy concessionary PT rates and are taxed at rates lower than non-owner-occupied ones.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: The new rates affect less than one in 10 owner-occupied residential properties.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: The AV is a proxy of the value of a property and is determined based on the rental transactions for comparable properties with similar attributes, such as location, age and condition.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: A property that earns more rental income has greater value.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: And therefore, the AV and the PT payable will be higher.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: The growth rate is similar for owner-occupied private residential properties within and outside the central region.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: I understand Members' concerns that some retirees may face financial difficulties.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: We do so not by lowering PT rates for residential properties owned by retirees, but by supporting our seniors in other ways.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: We have various schemes to help retirees, whether living in private residential properties or Housing and Development Board (HDB) flats.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: For example, through the Assurance Package (AP), seniors living in private properties can receive AP cash, AP MediSave and the cost-of-living special payment.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: How can the Government better help a particular group of retired seniors, who are private home residents but are cash poor, and would like to retire in the home that they have called "home" for decades?

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: In addition to what I mentioned, we also provide certain assistance and certain help schemes, that are applicable to all households, regardless of housing type.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: For example, the $300 Community Development Council (CDC) voucher that was given out in January this year, the Household Utilities Credit that was given out last year.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: And for seniors who are in the Merdeka Generation or the Pioneer Generation, they can also receive additional MediSave top-ups and healthcare subsidies when they visit the polyclinics, when they go see the general practitioner (GP), when they go to the hospital.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: And by that, what we mean is that everybody will contribute, but those who are wealthier and earn a higher income, will contribute more.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: As I mentioned in my reply earlier, the PT is a form of wealth tax on immovable assets.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: And if we look at the retirees who are staying in private properties, especially higher-end private properties with higher AVs, compared to retirees who are staying in rental flats or smaller HDB flats, I think there is a difference in their wealth.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I have one clarification for the Senior Minister of State.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Can the Ministry of Finance share, whether the Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore (IRAS) have a system to calibrate annual property values as a ratio of all owner- and tenant-occupied properties, to ensure that AVs are not disproportionately skewed by a few high rental units?

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: And so, I think this is a way to ensure that the data and the statistics are not skewed by some of these outliers.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: For some of these retirees, they do not see themselves as wealthy.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: I know they have got a property that may be worth quite a bit, but they are retirees with no income.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: They just had the luck of buying a property at a lower price when they were much younger.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: So, how do we want, as a matter of principle, to deal with this group of people who are living in a better property, but with no income?

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Is it the principle of the Government that we would want to persuade them to sell their property, so that they would not be considered wealthy?

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: I mean, how do we define the term "wealth"?

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Because I cannot see this group of retirees as being wealthy, except for the fact that they were fortunate enough to buy a property when they were younger.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: This does not mean, therefore, that we do not empathise with the situation that I am sure Mr Lim's residents face.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: I also have residents who are in a similar situation.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: I mentioned some examples earlier, in AP, and also when we look at certain schemes that we design.
